registration_flow: Clearance is initiated by the Executor.
GSI/Area In-charge signs just before the shift Fire Safety Officer (FSO).
FSO verifies all departmental clearances are complete.
FSO registers the document and retains the duplicate.
Clearance is officially issued only after registration at the Fire Station.

B_OISD_STD_105.mandatory_clearance: For excavation work regardless of depth, permission from all concerned sections must be obtained to protect underground facilities.
work_site_indicators: Markers must be physically placed around the boundaries of the proposed excavation.
Maximum excavation depth must be written on the permit.
B_OISD_STD_105.feedback_loop: A formal feedback communication system must notify all affected departments/sections once excavation work is completed.

8_underground_services_general_protectio.permission_and_survey: For excavation work regardless of depth (OISD) or below 30 cm (IS), complete underground clearance permissions must be obtained to locate and safeguard pipelines, sewers, cables, and utility lines.
8_underground_services_general_protectio.hand_digging_mandatory_zone: Under-digging or mechanical excavation is strictly prohibited around active lines. Only manual excavation using hand tools is permitted when working directly adjacent to identified underground assets.

32_work_instructions: If excavation is depth more than 1.5 mtr take confined space permit alongwith excavation permit.
Excavation work shall not be started unless clearance from all agencies are taken.
Separate work permit shall be taken for different agencies & locations.
A schematic drawing is to be attached if excavation activities likely to be extended more than one plant & in such cases separate work permit to be issued as applicable.
Excavation of earth for trenches or foundations shall be done uniformly in such a way that loose earth/material may not slide/fall on persons engaged in excavation work.
The loose material shall be put away (min. 1 m) and removed at earliest.
Vehicle movement nearby excavated area to be restricted.
The cutting of trenches shall be done only from top to bottom with adequate slope.
To avoid any danger of collapse of side material, the sides shall be secured properly.
The work shall be performed in such a way that only layers of earth are removed where underground cables pass. It shall be ensured that underground cables are not damaged while excavation.
Excavation job shall be carried out under supervision of Responsible Person.
Proper approach to digging area to be ensured at all times during job.
Extra precautions shall be taken by all concerned as may be necessary at time of excavation job.
Excavated area shall be properly secured with hard barrication and marked to avoid fall or trip.

dos: Ensure clearance has been obtained from various departments in prescribed form for all excavation works.
Ensure excavation permit and clearance has been obtained for excavation work and the same is valid.
All excavations and open trenches must be barricaded around opening. Warning lamp can be used for operating area and roads during darkness; use FLP type fixture in hazardous area.
There must be sufficient and safe means of access and escape for excavated sites.

Excavation area should be free from fumes/gases heavier than air because it may cause asphyxiation or poisoning. All excavation of depth more than 1.2 m or more should be treated as confined space and permit for entry into confined space should be obtained.
Excavation to a depth of 1 m or more shall be cut stepped back to give suitable slope or securely held by bracing to avoid danger of side collapse.

All trenches 1.2 m or more in depth shall at all times be equipped with at least one ladder for each 30.48 m length of excavation or fraction thereof. Ladders shall extend from bottom to at least 1 m above ground surface.
Barricading of 1 m height with red and white band/self-glowing caution boards should be carried out for excavation beyond 1.5 m depth.
All cutting shall be carried out from top to bottom.
Special precautions are required for mechanical excavators inside refinery because Hot Work Permit is required in operating areas except roads.
Practice of giving permission to cut half road and utilizing half road for vehicle movement should be avoided unless Donâ€™ts conditions are complied with.
Use suitable PPE as per job requirement mentioned in work permit.
Inform all incidents to supervisor and Fire Station immediately.
donts: Under no circumstances under cutting is to be carried out.
Excavated earth shall not be dumped within 1 m of edge or depth of trench whichever is more.

Excavated earth should not be dumped on nearby pathway/approaches, product/steam line, in front of emergency facilities such as fire hydrants/monitor, fire alarm points, inlet of foam pourers, or OWS manhole covers.
No vehicle should be allowed too close to edge because it may cause side collapse. Maintain at least 2 m distance from edge. Adequate and well-anchored stop blocks should be provided.
No mechanical excavation is to be carried out up to depth of 1.5 m from ground level in operating areas. Manual excavation is required up to 1.5 m.
No one should be allowed to move on edge of excavation.

title: Confined Space / Vessel Entry Extraction

confined_space_definitions.definition: An area not designed for continuous human occupancy, large enough for bodily entry and assigned work, with limited or restricted entry/exit, and which may or may not be enclosed.
An enclosure with known or potential hazards and restricted entrance/exit, not normally occupied, and usually not well ventilated.

typical_examples: Tanks, columns, reactors, boilers, boiler drums, sumps, spheres, bullets, bins, silos, reservoirs and surface condensers
Large-diameter piping/pipelines, flue ducts and HVAC ducts

Oil/water sewer pits, sewers, drain channels, column skirts, floating roof decks more than 3 m down from tank top, trenches, furnaces, flare stacks, gas turbine chambers, underground service lines, open-type vessels deeper than head level, and false ceilings/floors where oxygen deficiency or toxic/flammable gases are likely
Excavations or trenches deeper than 1.2 m

associated_permits: Excavation Permit for excavated pits deeper than 1.2 m

Trained entrants logged; training validity 1 year

Fresh air supplied; instrument air prohibited

Nearby nitrogen lines must be blinded to prevent accidental asphyxiation

purpose_and_scope: Ensure power-driven equipment, electrical switches and circuits are electrically safe and positively isolated before maintenance work.
Electrical repairs, troubleshooting (except minor non-process panel adjustments), switchgear maintenance, and HV/LV operations require a valid Electrical Work Permit.

C_De_energisation_Requirements: Confirm equipment is not in operation and request de-energisation.
Perform LOTO on the Local Switch before MCC isolation.
Confirm equipment is not operating at the local panel.
Verify all back-feeding circuits are isolated.
Switch off breaker control supply.
Switch off space heater supply unless Electrical Maintenance gives written instruction otherwise.
Switch breaker/MCC OFF.
Rack breaker out to isolated position.
Pull control circuit fuses.
Pull main power fuses.
Close and secure front and back panel lids.
Visually inspect breaker/switch internals.
Discharge isolated line to earth and perform physical voltage test.
Provide temporary safety earthing/grounding on load side where required.
Perform LOTO on breaker/MCC panel.
D_Re_energisation_Requirements: Confirm work is complete, applicable permits are closed, locks/tags removed, equipment earthing intact, and request re-energisation.
Conduct and record Insulation Resistance (IR) test.
Box up and secure breaker panel lids/covers.
Ensure breaker closing spring is not charged before racking in.
Return Local/Remote switch to Remote position.
E_LOTO_and_Danger_Tags: Electrical isolation, switch lockout and DANGER tagging are mandatory before permit issue.
Danger tags must be signed, dated and show exact isolation time.
Each participating maintenance, operation and contractor agency applies its own LOTO locks and tags.
Aarti Industries records Tag No., Name and Sign for local switch isolation.
Every LOTO/isolation action must be recorded in the electrical shift logbook.
Tags are removed and logbook records updated after work completion and permit closure.

electrical_protection: Shock-proof rubber gloves; verify expiry date before use.
Approved rubber matting or insulated platform at switchgear/panels.
Wooden platform, insulated stand or wooden ladder for elevated electrical access.
Certified joint-free electrical cables and properly insulated hand tools.

Part_I: Authorized Person of Electrical Operation certification
Part_II: Authorized Person of Electrical Operation certification

H_Restoration_and_Document_Control: Authorized Person of Electrical Operation completes the Job Completion Certificate after confirming the worksite is clear.
Executing agency certifies all tools, equipment, manpower and unused materials are removed and the area is cleaned.
Equipment earthing/grounding must be visually checked and intact before restoration.
Back-feed circuits are normalized only during the final checklist stage.
Clearance certificate is issued in duplicate: white and pink copies.
Original white copy is returned to Operation-In-Charge; pink copy is retained by Electrical Operation.
No operational activity may be authorized until the signed original white isolation copy is returned.
I_Dos: Obtain a valid Electrical Isolation/Energisation Permit before electrical work.
Perform LOTO on the Local Switch before requesting MCC isolation.
Attach signed, dated and timed DANGER/DO NOT OPERATE tags.
Verify discharge and perform a physical voltage test.
Use wooden platform, rubber matting or insulated stand at panels/switchgear.
Connect portable/mobile electrical equipment to an ELCB.
Check shock-proof glove expiry before use.
Use joint-free, sound-insulation electrical cables.
Inspect switch internals and report damage.
Remove tools, equipment, manpower and scrap on completion.
I_Donts: Never work on electrical switchgear without verifying control and power fuses are physically pulled.
Do not wear loose or synthetic clothing during electrical work.
Do not bypass or keep motor space heaters ON during isolation unless specifically authorized in writing.
Do not rack in a breaker with a charged closing spring.
Do not use electrode holders as cable connectors for welding cable extensions.
Do not use standard 230 V hand lamps inside confined spaces.
Do not authorize operation of isolated equipment until the electrical department returns the original white isolation copy.

dos: Ensure clearance obtained from various departments in prescribed form for all excavation works.

sections.title: DO'S AND DON'TS DURING EXCAVATION WORK (ANNEX D-26)
dos: Ensure clearance from various departments in prescribed form for all excavation works.
Ensure excavation permit and clearance obtained and valid.
Barricade all excavations/open trenches; use warning lamp during darkness and FLP fixture in hazardous area.
Provide sufficient and safe access and escape.
Keep excavation free from fumes/gases heavier than air; treat excavation more than 1.2 m as confined space and obtain entry permit.
For excavation 1 m or more, cut stepped back to suitable slope or secure with bracing.
For trenches 1.2 m or more, provide at least one ladder per 30.48 m length/fraction; extend ladder at least 1 m above ground.
For excavation beyond 1.5 m, provide 1 m high barricading with red/white band or self-glowing caution boards.
Carry out all cutting from top to bottom.
Mechanical excavators inside refinery require special precautions and Hot Work Permit in operating areas except roads.
Avoid half-road cutting and half-road vehicle movement unless required conditions are met.
Use suitable PPE as required by work permit.
Report all incidents to supervisor and Fire Station immediately.
donts: Under no circumstances carry out under-cutting.
Do not dump excavated earth within 1 m of edge or trench depth, whichever is more.
Do not dump excavated earth on pathways/approaches, product/steam lines, emergency facilities or OWS manhole covers.
Do not allow vehicles too close to edge; maintain at least 2 m and provide anchored stop blocks.
Do not mechanically excavate up to 1.5 m in operating areas; manual excavation required to 1.5 m.
Do not allow anyone to move on the edge of excavation.

7_permittee_executor.declaration: I certify that all necessary precautions are taken to carry out work in safe manner. I understand the work site has been prepared for safe work, I understand the precautions & shall ensure the same are followed by the working working crew. If change in conditions are observed or instructed, the work shall be stopped & issuer would be notified.

8_underground_services_general_protectio.permission_survey: For excavation work regardless of depth (OISD) or below 30 cm (IS), complete underground clearance permissions must be obtained to locate and safeguard pipelines, sewers, cables, and utility lines.
8_underground_services_general_protectio.hand_digging_zone: Under-digging or mechanical excavation is strictly prohibited around active lines. Only manual excavation using hand tools is permitted when working directly adjacent to identified underground assets.
8_underground_services_general_protectio.utility_map_reference: Attach site-specific marked-up schematic drawing and site layout showing all buried lines.

9_cables.IS_17893_D_17: UNDERGROUND POWER CABLE must be identified as existing/not existing. Precautions include isolation, LOTO, and physical site-marking.
9_cables.Aarti_A2: If underground cables are present, they must be de-energised and checked by underground cable tracer before floor-breaking.
9_cables.Aarti_instruction_10: Only layers of earth are removed where underground cables pass and underground cables must not be damaged.

10_pipelines.IS_17893_D_22: UNDERGROUND PRODUCT LINE, UTILITY LINE checklist must be signed off by Operations Group.
10_pipelines.OISD_5_0_v: Clearance must protect sewers, storm drains, and CBD channels. Dyke cutting is extremely critical due to risk of major hydrocarbon spills.
10_pipelines.Aarti_D1: Operations Group verifies excavation area is free of process lines, steam/utility pipes, toxic chemical seepage, and sewage lines.

11_firewater_lines.IS_17893_D_19: Underground firewater line clearance checks; maintain minimum safe distance and identify pipe depth.
11_firewater_lines.Aarti_C: Fire/Safety Group declares area safe; fire water mains must not be disturbed and access to nearby fire hydrants must remain unhindered.

12_communication_cables.IS_17893_D_18: UNDERGROUND TELECOMMUNICATION CABLE clearance must be obtained and signed off by Telecom/IT.

13_instrument_cables.IS_17893_D_23: UNDERGROUND INSTRUMENT CABLE must be checked and cleared by Instrumentation Department.
13_instrument_cables.Aarti_B: Instrumentation Group verifies IT and signal cable status. Cable de-energisation is mandatory if they lie directly within excavation zone.

14_cathodic_protection_cables.IS_17893_D_24: UNDERGROUND CATHODIC PROTECTION CABLE checklist requires verifying CP cable existence and listing precautions to prevent severing anodes or wiring.

15_manual_excavation.IS_17893_Table_14_iv: Hand excavation only can be checked as a binding requirement.
15_manual_excavation.IS_17893_D_26_2_5: Manual excavation is compulsory up to a depth of 1.5 meters from ground level in operating plant areas.
15_manual_excavation.Aarti_D2: Permit toggle Manual restricts contractor to hand shovels and pickaxes.

16_mechanical_excavation.IS_17893_D_26_1_10: Special precautions are required for mechanical excavators inside refinery; Hot Work Permit required in operating areas except roads.
16_mechanical_excavation.IS_17893_D_26_2_5: No mechanical excavation up to 1.5 m from ground level in plant operating areas.
16_mechanical_excavation.Aarti_instruction_11: Excavation job shall be carried out under supervision of Responsible Person.
16_mechanical_excavation.Aarti_D2: Mechanical toggle includes JCB/floor breaker and requires Hot Work Permit and JSA due to internal combustion engine spark hazards.

17_shoring.IS_17893_D_26_1_6: Excavations to a depth of 1 m or more must be securely held by bracing/shoring.
17_shoring.Aarti_E7: Shoring provided if depth exceed 5 ft.
17_shoring.Aarti_instruction_9: Sides shall be secured properly to avoid collapse.

18_sloping.IS_17893_Table_14_ix: Batter sides to 45 degree or less checkbox.
18_sloping.IS_17893_D_26_1_6: Excavations of 1 m or more deep must be stepped back to a suitable safe slope.
18_sloping.Aarti_instruction_8: Cutting trenches only from top to bottom with adequate slope.

19_benching.IS_17893_D_26_1_6: For trenches of 1 m or more, ground must be stepped back/benched or sloped.
19_benching.Aarti_instruction_5: Excavation for trenches/foundations shall be uniform so loose earth/material does not slide/fall on workers.

20_access_escape.IS_17893_D_26_1_4: Sufficient and safe means of access and escape required.
20_access_escape.Aarti_instruction_12: Proper approach to digging area ensured at all times.

21_ladder.IS_17893_D_26_1_7: Trenches 1.2 m or more deep require at least one ladder per 30.48 m length or fraction.
21_ladder.extension_rule: Ladders extend from trench bottom to at least 1 m above ground surface.
21_ladder.Aarti_E1: Layout must include shoring, sloping and escape ladder arrangements.

22_barricading.IS_17893_D_26_1_8: Hard barricading of 1 m height with red/white band or self-glowing caution boards mandatory for excavation beyond 1.5 m.
22_barricading.Aarti_E12: Area cordoned and caution boards provided.
22_barricading.Aarti_instruction_14: Excavated area properly secured with hard barricading and marked to avoid fall/trip.

23_warning_lights.IS_17893_Table_14_vi: Provide flashing light; flameproof in hazardous area.
23_warning_lights.IS_17893_D_26_1_3: Warning lamp can be used in operating area and roads during darkness; use FLP fixture in hazardous area.

24_spoil_pile.IS_17893_Table_14_xii: Excavated soil 1 m away from edge, minimum.
24_spoil_pile.IS_17893_D_26_2_2: Excavated earth shall not be dumped within 1 m of excavation edge or trench depth, whichever is more.
24_spoil_pile.IS_17893_D_26_2_3: Never dump earth on pathways/approaches, product/steam lines, or in front of emergency facilities including fire hydrants/monitors, fire alarm points, foam pourer inlets and OWS manhole covers.
24_spoil_pile.Aarti_instruction_6: Loose material shall be put away minimum 1 m and removed at earliest.

25_vehicle_movement.IS_17893_D_26_2_4: Vehicles must maintain at least 2 m from excavation edge.
25_vehicle_movement.stop_blocks: Adequate, well-anchored stop blocks must prevent vehicles from entering/reversing into excavation.
25_vehicle_movement.Aarti_instruction_7: Vehicle movement near excavated area to be restricted.

26_road_dyke_cutting.IS_17893_D_25_9_D_25_10: Road cutting requires Excavation Clearance and dedicated Road Closure Format submitted to Fire Station at least one day before work; barricading, precautionary signs and alternate routes required.
26_road_dyke_cutting.OISD_5_0_v_dyke: Dyke cutting requires elevated authorization due to severe process hazard and dyke must be reconstructed in shortest possible time.

27_gas_testing.IS_17893_D_26_1_5: Excavation must be verified free from fumes or gases heavier than air.

28_confined_space_escalation.OISD_4_3: Any excavation more than 1.2 m depth must be treated as confined space.
28_confined_space_escalation.IS_17893_D_26_1_5: All excavation of depth more than 1.2 m or more should be treated as confined space and confined-space entry permit obtained.
28_confined_space_escalation.Aarti_instruction_1: If excavation depth is more than 1.5 m, take confined space permit along with excavation permit.

29_PPE.IS_17893_Annex_D_Note_5: Helmet, safety shoes, boiler suit and hand gloves mandatory for all excavation works.

30_JSA.IS_17893_Annex_D_Note_6: Daily Safety Toolbox Talks based on JSA must be conducted for contractor personnel before starting work and records maintained.
30_JSA.Aarti_D3: JSA attached with sketch including shoring, sloping and escape ladder arrangements; JSA reference number and date written at bottom.

31_drawing_layout.IS_17893_D_1_2: Marked-up schematic drawing showing exact cutting bounds must be attached.
31_drawing_layout.IS_17893_D_14: SKETCH OF THE AREA OF EXCAVATION ENCLOSED checkbox.
31_drawing_layout.Aarti_D1: Layout attached with permit with marking is mandatory.

32_aarti_work_instructions: If excavation is depth more than 1.5 mtr take confined space permit alongwith excavation permit.
Excavation work shall not be started unless the clearance from all the agencies are taken.
Separate work permit shall be taken for different agencies & locations.
A schematic drawing is to be attached if excavation activities likely to be extended more than one plant & in such cases separate work permit to be issued as applicable.
Excavation of earth for trenches or foundations shall be done uniformly in such a way that loose earth/material may not slide/fall on persons engaged in excavation work.
The loose material shall be put away (min. 1 m) and removed at earliest.
Vehicle movement nearby excavated area to be restricted.
The cutting of trenches shall be done only from top to bottom with adequate slope.
To avoid any danger of collapse of side material, the sides shall be secured properly.
The work shall be performed so that only layers of earth are removed where underground cables pass and underground cables are not damaged.
Excavation job shall be carried out under supervision of Responsible Person.
Proper approach to digging area shall be ensured at all times during job.
Extra precautions shall be taken by all concerned as necessary at time of excavation.
Excavated area shall be properly secured with hard barricading and marked to avoid fall or trip.

33_renewal.IS_17893_Annex_D_Note_4: Permits maximum 7 days but must be renewed in each shift.
33_renewal.Aarti_renewal_block: All precautionary measures reviewed and found OK; Date; Time From/To; Permittee, Issuer and Plant Manager signatures.

34_closure.IS_17893_D_25_8: On completion receiver collects all clearance copies and encloses them with closed permit; Issuer closes permit and returns it to Fire Station.
34_closure.Aarti_closure_block: Closure of Work Permit with Date & Time, Production Dept Sign, Mech./Elect./Civil/Inst. Dept Sign, confirmation that safety devices are replaced and area cleaned.

dos: Ensure clearance obtained from various departments in prescribed form for all excavation works.
Ensure excavation permit and clearance are obtained and valid.
All excavations/open trenches must be barricaded; warning lamp may be used during darkness and FLP fixture in hazardous areas.
Provide sufficient and safe means of access and escape.
Ensure excavation is free from fumes/gases heavier than air; excavation more than 1.2 m should be treated as confined space and entry permit obtained.
Excavation 1 m or more shall be sloped/stepped back or securely shored.
Trenches 1.2 m or more require at least one ladder per 30.48 m length, extending at least 1 m above ground.
Barricade 1 m high with red/white band or self-glowing caution boards for excavation beyond 1.5 m.
All cutting shall be from top to bottom.
Special precautions and Hot Work Permit required for mechanical excavators in refinery operating areas except roads.
Avoid half-road cutting unless specified conditions are met.
Use suitable PPE as per permit.
Report all incidents to supervisor and Fire Station immediately.
donts: Under no circumstances shall undercutting be carried out.
Do not dump excavated earth within 1 m of edge or trench depth, whichever is more.
Do not dump excavated earth on pathways, product/steam lines, emergency facilities or OWS manhole covers.
Do not allow vehicles too close to excavation edge; maintain at least 2 m and provide anchored stop blocks.
No mechanical excavation up to 1.5 m in operating areas; manual excavation required.
No one should move on edge of excavation.

depth_limits_and_escalations.30_cm: Excavation Permit mandatory below 30 cm; up to 30 cm can be under Cold Work Permit.
depth_limits_and_escalations.1.2_m: Depth threshold for confined-space treatment under IS/OISD.
depth_limits_and_escalations.1.5_m_mechanical: Maximum depth at which mechanical excavation is prohibited in operating plant areas.

access_egress.30.48_m: Maximum trench length interval per ladder.

clearances.1.0_m_barricade: Minimum hard barricade height for excavations beyond 1.5 m.

document_control.30_days: Maximum validity for major construction projects.
document_control.1_shift: Maximum operational duration before shift renewal.
document_control.15_days_clearance: Maximum excavation clearance validity at operating facilities.
document_control.1_month_clearance: Maximum excavation clearance validity at construction/non-operating sites.
document_control.1_day_advance_permit: Permit must be obtained at least one day in advance.
document_control.1_day_road_closure: Road closure format submitted at least one day before road cutting.

subsections.title: A. Contractor Employee PTW System Exposure
content: Because several maintenance and construction tasks are performed with assistance from contractors, OISD-STD-105 mandates that operating facilities must provide sufficient exposure to both the contractor and his employees on the work permit system [OISD Cl. 5.0(x)].

subsections.title: B. Permit Issuance Restriction to Contractors
content: Work permits **must never be directly issued to a contractor**. IS 17893 mandates that the work permit must bear the name and designation of a company employee (from maintenance, construction, project, or construction disciplines) who will act as the permit holder/receiver [IS Cl. 4.1.1-e, 7.3.1].
lists: *Direct Contractor Issuance Exception*: In small, remote installations where an independent company supervisor is not present on-site, the local Owner-In-Charge may issue the permit to the contractor's authorized supervisor directly and obtain their physical signature [OISD Cl. 5.0(g)].

subsections.title: C. Direct Contractor Responsibilities
numbered_items: 1.  **Requisite PPE Provision**: The contract supervisor is solely responsible for purchasing and providing all required specialized personal protective equipment (PPE) to their workers [IS 7.3.1.7-c].

2.  **Compliance with Permit Safeguards**: The contractor supervisor and contract workers must ensure that all precautions, gas-test safety zones, and barriers specified in the work permit are strictly maintained at the site at all times [IS 7.3.1.7-a].

3.  **Site Housekeeping**: The contract supervisor must ensure that all scrap, leftover materials, and scaffolding are fully removed and housekeeping is restored to normal before requesting permit closure [IS 7.3.1.8].

4.  **Deviations Notification**: The contract supervisor must immediately stop work and notify the company's area operator and executor if job conditions deviate from safe operational limits [IS 7.3.1.7-b].

sections.title: 3. COMPULSORY TOOLBOX TALKS & SAFETY BRIEFINGS
lists: **Toolbox Talk (Safety Talk) Mandate**: Prior to starting any job, the company permit receiver/executor must conduct a formal safety toolbox talk to all contract and departmental workers [IS 7.3.1.6, Annex D Cl. D-137 Note 6].
**Content of Briefing**: The safety talk must:

**Site Register Record-Keeping**: The Permittee must maintain a dedicated site register for the toolbox talk. This register must be physically signed by all workers and supervisors associated with the work before commencement of each shift [IS B-6.18].

**100% Briefing Check**: The permit issuer must verify that a "100 percent safety briefing [has been] given by Site engineer before start of work" on the pre-erection scaffolding checklists [IS Table 20 Sl v].
numbered_items: 1.  Emphasize the step-by-step procedures for safe job execution [IS 7.3.1.6].
2.  Identify all local process hazards, toxic gases, or high-pressure steam risks [IS 7.3.1.6].
3.  Explain all permit safeguards, emergency escape routes, and siren codes [IS 7.3.1.6, A-7.1.18].

subsections.title: A. The Master Authorization List
content: Every process plant or manufacturing unit must maintain a current, printed **list of employees who are authorized to sign, issue, or receive work permits** [IS 7.2.2, 7.3.1].
lists: *Publisher*: Respective Plant HOD or Area In-Charge [IS 12.2.2].

*Validation Process*: The HOD Safety coordinates with individual plant HODs to train and validate all candidates [IS 12.1.1]. The HOD Safety develops procedures and training materials for validation [IS 12.1.3]. Once validated, the plant HOD officially publishes the names in the prescribed format [IS 12.2.2].

subsections.title: B. Medical Fitness Requirements
lists: **Working at Height**: Mandatory physical and clinical evaluation is required for all personnel working at heights of **2.0 meters and above** (including fragile roofs, chimney repairs, and elevated structures) [IS Table 20 Sl viii].
**Medical Certificate**: A registered medical practitioner must examine the worker and issue a signed certificate (Form F-20.1) verifying the worker is fit to work at heights [IS F-18.1].
**Medical Exclusion Criteria**: Workers must be clinically certified as free from height-inhibiting diseases, including:
numbered_items: 1.  **Vertigo** (dizziness or equilibrium loss).
2.  **Epilepsy** or history of fits.
3.  General giddiness or sudden blackouts.
4.  Abnormal blood pressure (B.P.) or unstable pulse rate.
5.  Impaired eyesight.

subsections.title: C. General Record Keeping and Archiving
lists: **IS 17893 Archive Rule**: The original/acceptor copy of all closed work permits must be filed and kept by the issuing department for a period of **at least 30 days** from the date of permit closure [IS Section 13].

**OISD-STD-105 Archive Rule**: Copies of completed or used permits must be properly filed and kept as records for a period of **at least 3 months** from the date of job completion or successful commissioning of the facility, whichever is later [OISD Cl. 5.0(w)].
**Toolbox Talk Records**: Signed shift toolbox talk registers must be archived locally at the site office as an administrative record [IS B-6.18].

subsections.title: A. Permit Issuer (Shift In-Charge / Owner-In-Charge)
lists: **Required Training**: Minimum 1-day initial PTW training course; minimum 1-day retraining once every 2 years [OISD 5.0(x)].
**Signature Responsibility**: Signs the permit request, clearance renewals/revalidations, and permit closure block [IS A-5].
**Key Responsibilities**:
**Authority Constraints**: **No person is permitted to issue a work permit to himself** [IS 7.2.1; OISD 5.0(f)].
numbered_items: 1.  Maintains ultimate control over the entire work permit process in his operating area [IS 7.2.3-a].
2.  Ensures equipment isolation, cleaning, de-pressurisation, and gas tests are fully complete [IS 7.2.3-b].
3.  Obtains final authorization from the plant HOD/area in-charge for critical permits (hot work, entry, excavation) before hand-over [IS 7.2.3-f].
4.  Performs an independent risk assessment for highly complex or infrequent tasks [IS 7.2.3-b].
5.  Reviews ongoing permits during shift handovers and immediately suspends work if unsafe conditions develop [IS 7.2.3-e, 7.5.5].

subsections.title: B. Permit Receiver / Executor (Company Supervisor)
lists: **Required Training**: Minimum 1-day initial PTW training course; minimum 1-day retraining once every 2 years [OISD 5.0(x)].
**Signature Responsibility**: Signs permit request, joint inspection certificates, revalidation requests (backside), and job completion box [IS 7.3.1.3, A-5].
**Key Responsibilities**:
**Authority Constraints**: Direct contractor supervisors are prohibited from accepting permits, except in small, remote installations where no company engineering supervisor exists [OISD Cl. 5.0(g)].
numbered_items: 1.  Maintains direct accountability for the safe execution of the maintenance or construction task [IS 7.3.1.2].
2.  Performs a joint site inspection with the permit issuer to verify physical isolations and recommend specialized PPE [IS 7.3.1.1].
3.  Conducts mandatory daily safety toolbox talks and maintains the signed site register [IS B-6.18].
4.  Ensures the contractor supervisor provides certified, quality hand tools and standard PPE [IS 7.3.1.7-c, 7.3.1.12].
5.  Visually inspects and restores housekeeping, gratings, and guards to normal before signing for closure [IS 7.3.1.8].

subsections.title: C. Confined Space Standby Attendant (Standby Person)
lists: **Required Training**: Safety training on confined space hazards, personal gas monitors, communication devices, rescue procedures, andentrant headcount logging. Training validity is **exactly 1 year** [IS C-3].
**Signature Responsibility**: Signs the confined space entrant attendance register (IS Table 13) to log entrants in and out [IS C-15 Note 1].
**Key Responsibilities**:

**Authority Constraints**: **"Do not give any other responsibility to stand by person, which may cause his absence at man way"** [IS C-14.2.2]. The standby person is strictly prohibited from entering the space to perform a rescue unless physically relieved by another trained attendant and wearing an SCBA [ptw aarti Standby Rule 16, image 85].
numbered_items: 1.  Remains physically stationed at the manway/entry point at all times while anyone is inside [IS C-14.1.7].
2.  Maintains constant touch and communication with the entrants to monitor their physical condition [IS C-14.1.8].
3.  Maintains an accurate, real-time headcount and log of all personnel entering and exiting [IS C-15 Note 1].
4.  Summons rescue teams and coordinates emergency equipment (SCBA, tripods, resuscitators) in case of distress [IS C-14.1.8].

subsections.title: D. Scaffold Supervisor
lists: **Required Training**: Specialized training on scaffolding stability, joint pinning, ledgers, transoms, base/sole plates, climbing angles, and load limits. Training validity is **exactly 1 year** [IS F-17].
**Signature Responsibility**: Enderses the pre-erection checklist (IS Table 20) and signs/dates the **Green Tag** displayed on-site [IS F-8-i, ii].
**Key Responsibilities**:
numbered_items: 1.  Personally supervises the erection, modification, and dismantling of all scaffolding [IS F-17].
2.  Conducts detailed physical inspections of scaffolding poles, couplers, platforms, and foundations.
3.  Certifies and attaches a Green Tag to safe scaffolds, or hangs a Red Tag on incomplete structures [IS F-8-i, ii].
4.  Conducts weekly structural re-certifications of all standing scaffolding [IS F-8-iii].

sections.title: 6. TYPOS & ANOMALIES
lists: **IS 17893 Cl. 12.1.1 (Page 46)**: Uses awkward spacing in formatting: "...train and validate all people involved in the signing of work permit procedures..." [12.1.1].
**IS 17893 Cl. B-6.18 (Page 21)**: Typo spells "permittee" as **"permittee"** and "toolbox" as **"tool box"** ("Daily tool box talk...").
**IS 17893 Cl. C-3 (Page 23)**: Plural/singular typo: "The Name of Trained Attendant for Entry (Training Validity 1 Year) as specified in Table 8" (lists spaces for multiple attendants) [C-3].

sections.title: UNDERGROUND SERVICES GENERAL PROTECTION
requirements: For excavation work regardless of depth (OISD) or below 30 cm (IS), complete underground clearance permissions must be obtained to locate and safeguard pipelines, sewers, cables, and utility lines.

Under-digging or mechanical excavation is strictly prohibited around active lines. Only manual excavation using hand tools is permitted when working directly adjacent to identified underground assets.
Executers must attach a site-specific marked-up schematic drawing and site layout showing all buried lines.

sections.title: BURIAL DETAIL: CABLES
requirements: IS 17893 D-17: UNDERGROUND POWER CABLE must be identified as existing/not existing; precautions include isolation, LOTO and physical site-marking.
Aarti Part-I Section A.2: If underground cables are present, they must be de-energised and checked by underground cable tracer before floor-breaking.
Aarti Work Instruction 10: Only layers of earth where underground cables pass should be removed and cables must not be damaged.

sections.title: BURIAL DETAIL: PIPELINES
requirements: IS 17893 D-22: UNDERGROUND PRODUCT LINE, UTILITY LINE checklist must be signed off by Operations Group.
OISD-STD-105 Cl. 5.0(v): Clearance must protect sewers, storm drains and CBD channels. Dyke cutting is extremely critical due to risk of major hydrocarbon spills to outer bunds.
Aarti Part-I Section D.1: Operations Group must verify area is free of process lines, steam/utility pipes, toxic chemical seepage and sewage lines.

sections.title: BURIAL DETAIL: FIREWATER LINES
requirements: IS 17893 D-19: Underground firewater line clearance checks; precautions require minimum safe distance and identifying pipe depth.
Aarti Part-I Section C: Fire/Safety Group checks and declares area safe; firewater mains must not be disturbed and access to nearby hydrants must remain unhindered.

sections.title: BURIAL DETAIL: COMMUNICATION CABLES
requirements: IS 17893 D-18: UNDERGROUND TELECOMMUNICATION CABLE clearance must be obtained and signed off by Telecom/IT section.
OISD-STD-105 Cl. 4.2: Telephone line preservation is required during excavation.

sections.title: BURIAL DETAIL: INSTRUMENT CABLES
requirements: IS 17893 D-23: UNDERGROUND INSTRUMENT CABLE must be checked and cleared by Instrumentation Department.
Aarti Part-I Section B: Instrumentation Group verifies IT and signal cable status; cable de-energisation is mandatory if directly within excavation zone.

sections.title: BURIAL DETAIL: CATHODIC PROTECTION (CP) CABLES
requirements: IS 17893 D-24: UNDERGROUND CATHODIC PROTECTION CABLE checklist requires verifying CP cable existence.
Dedicated precautions must be listed to prevent severing anodes or wiring.

sections.title: MANUAL EXCAVATION
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl iv: Hand excavation only can be checked as a binding requirement under associated permit safety rules.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.2.5: Manual excavation is compulsory up to a depth of 1.5 meters from ground level in all operating plant areas.
Aarti Part-I Section D.2: Permit toggles Manual to restrict contractor to hand shovels and pickaxes.

sections.title: MECHANICAL EXCAVATION
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.10: Special precautions are required for mechanical excavators inside refinery because Hot Work Permit is required in operating refinery areas except roads.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.2.5: No mechanical excavation is permitted up to a depth of 1.5 m from ground level in plant operating areas.
Aarti Work Instruction 11: Excavation job shall be carried out under supervision of Responsible Person.
Aarti Part-I Section D.2: Mechanical (e.g. JCB, floor breaker etc.) requires Hot Work Permit and JSA due to internal combustion engine spark hazards.

sections.title: SHORING
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl viii: Provide shoring checkbox.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.6: Excavations to a depth of 1 m or more must be securely held by bracing/shoring to avoid side collapse.
Aarti Part-II Section E.7: Shoring provided if depth exceeds 5 ft.
Aarti Work Instruction 9: Sides shall be secured properly to avoid danger of collapse.

sections.title: SLOPING
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl ix: Batter sides to 45 degree or less.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.6: Excavations of 1 m or more must be cut stepped back to a suitable safe slope.
Aarti Work Instruction 8: Cutting trenches shall be from top to bottom with adequate slope.

sections.title: BENCHING
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.6: For trenches 1 m or more deep, ground must be stepped back/benched or sloped to prevent collapse.
Aarti Work Instruction 5: Trenches/foundations shall be excavated uniformly so loose earth/material does not slide/fall on workers.

sections.title: ACCESS / ESCAPE
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl xi: Provide means of access.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.4: Sufficient and safe means of access and escape must be provided.
Aarti Work Instruction 12: Proper approach to digging area must be ensured at all times.

sections.title: LADDER
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.7: All trenches 1.2 m or more deep require at least one ladder per 30.48 m length or fraction.
Ladders must extend from trench bottom to at least 1 m above ground.
Aarti Part-II Section E.1: Layout must include escape ladder arrangements.

sections.title: BARRICADING
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl vii: Barricade checkbox.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.8: Hard barricading of 1 m height with red/white band or self-glowing caution boards is mandatory for excavation beyond 1.5 m depth.
Aarti Part-II Section E.12: Area cordoned and caution boards provided.
Aarti Work Instruction 14: Excavated area shall be secured with hard barricading and marked to avoid falls/trips.

sections.title: WARNING LIGHTS
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl vi: Provide flashing light, flameproof in hazardous area.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.3: Warning lamp can be used in operating areas and roads during darkness; FLP fixture in hazardous area.

sections.title: SPOIL PILE (EXCAVATED EARTH)
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl xii: Excavated soil 1 m away from edge, minimum.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.2.2: Excavated earth shall not be dumped within 1 m of excavation edge or depth of trench, whichever is more.

IS 17893 Cl. D-26.2.3: Never dump excavated earth on nearby pathways/approaches, product/steam lines, or in front of emergency facilities including hydrants/monitors, fire alarm points, foam pourer inlets and OWS manhole covers.
Aarti Work Instruction 6: Loose material shall be put away minimum 1 m and removed at earliest.

sections.title: VEHICLE MOVEMENT
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-26.2.4: Vehicles must maintain at least 2 m from excavation edge.
Adequate, well-anchored stop blocks must prevent vehicles from being driven/reversed into excavation.
Aarti Work Instruction 7: Vehicle movement near excavated area must be restricted.

sections.title: ROAD / DYKE CUTTING
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-25.9/D-25.10: Road cutting requires Excavation Clearance and dedicated Road Closure Format.
Road Closure Format must be submitted to Fire Station at least one day before work.
Cuttings must be properly barricaded with precautionary signs and alternate routes displayed.
OISD-STD-105 Cl. 5.0(v): Dyke cutting requires high-level designated authority authorization due to bund failure/hydrocarbon spill risk.
Dyke must be reconstructed in the shortest possible time.

sections.title: GAS TESTING
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.5: Excavation must be verified free from fumes or gases heavier than air.
Aarti Part-II Section E.8: Gas testing required when trench depth is greater than 1.5 m.
Tests: H2S, O2, CO and LEL%.
Test records at 0 Hrs, 4 Hrs and 6 Hrs.

sections.title: CONFINED-SPACE ESCALATION
requirements: OISD-STD-105 Cl. 4.3: Excavation deeper than 1.2 m must be treated as confined space.
IS 17893 Cl. D-26.1.5: Excavation depth more than 1.2 m or more should be treated as confined space and confined-space entry permit obtained.
Aarti Work Instruction 1: If excavation depth is more than 1.5 m, take confined space permit along with excavation permit.

sections.title: PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
requirements: IS 17893 Table 14 Sl xiv/xv: Body harness/lifeline and gumboot/safety suit toggles.
IS 17893 Annex D Note 5: Helmet, safety shoes, boiler suit and hand gloves are mandatory for all excavation works.
Aarti Part-II Section E.11: PPE provided and use ensured.

sections.title: JOB SAFETY ANALYSIS (JSA)
requirements: IS 17893 Annex D Note 6: Daily Safety Toolbox Talks with key-point safety tips based on JSA must be conducted for contractor personnel before work; formal records maintained.
Aarti Part-I Section D.3: JSA attached with sketch diagram including shoring, sloping and escape ladder arrangements: Yes / No / NA.
JSA reference number and date must be written at bottom.

sections.title: DRAWING / LAYOUT
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-1.2: Marked-up schematic drawing showing exact cutting bounds must be attached.
IS 17893 Cl. D-14: SKETCH OF THE AREA OF EXCAVATION ENCLOSED checkbox.
Aarti Part-I Section D.1: Layout attached with permit with marking is mandatory.

sections.title: WORK INSTRUCTIONS
instructions: 1. If excavation is depth more than 1.5 mtr take confined space permit alongwith excavation permit.
2. Excavation work shall not be started unless the clearance from all the agencies are taken.
3. Separate work permit shall be taken for different agencies & locations.
4. A schematic drawing is to be attached if excavation activities likely to be extended more than one plant & in such cases separate work permit to be issued as applicable.
5. Excavation of earth for trenches or foundations shall be done uniformly in such a way that loose earth /material may not slide/ fall on the persons engaged in excavation work.
6. The loose material shall be put away(min. 1 m) and removed at earliest.
7. Vehicle movement nearby excavated area to be restricted.
8. The cutting of trenches shall be done only from top to bottom with adequate slope.
9. To avoid any danger of collapse of side material, the sides shall be secured properly.
10. The work shall be performed in such a way that only layers of the earth are removed where underground cables pass. It shall be ensured that underground cables are not damaged while excavation.
11. Excavation job shall be carried out under the supervision of Responsible Person.
12. Proper approach to the digging area to be ensured at all the time during job.
13. Extra precautions shall be taken by all the concerned as may be necessary at the time of excavation job.
14. Excavated area shall be properly secured with hard barrication and marked to avoid fall or trip.

sections.title: RENEWAL
requirements: IS 17893 Annex D Note 4: Permits issued for maximum 7 days but must be renewed in each shift.
Aarti Overleaf Renewal Block: All precautionary measures reviewed and found O.K.; Date; Time From/To; signatures of Permittee, Issuer and Plant Manager.

sections.title: CLOSURE
requirements: IS 17893 Cl. D-25.8: On completion, receiver collects all clearance copies and encloses them with closed permit. Issuer closes permit and returns it to Fire Station.
Aarti Overleaf Closure Block: Closure of Work Permit with Date & Time, Production Dept Sign, Mech./Elect./Civil/Inst. Dept Sign.
Confirmation that all safety devices are replaced and area cleaned.

sections.title: DO'S AND DON'TS DURING EXCAVATION WORK
dos: Ensure clearance from various departments in prescribed form for all excavation works.
Ensure excavation permit and clearance are obtained and valid.
All excavations/open trenches must be barricaded; warning lamp may be used during darkness, FLP fixture in hazardous area.
Provide sufficient and safe access and escape.
Ensure excavation is free from fumes/gases heavier than air. Excavation more than 1.2 m or more should be treated as confined space and confined-space permit obtained.
Excavation 1 m or more shall be stepped back to suitable slope or securely braced.
Trenches 1.2 m or more require ladder per 30.48 m or fraction, extending at least 1 m above ground.
Barricading 1 m high with red/white band or self-glowing caution boards for excavation beyond 1.5 m.
All cutting shall be from top to bottom.
Special precautions for mechanical excavators inside refinery; Hot Work Permit required in operating refinery areas except roads.
Avoid permission to cut half road and use half road unless specified Donâ€™ts conditions are met.
Use suitable PPE as per job requirement.
Inform all incidents to supervisor and Fire Station immediately.
donts: Under no circumstances is undercutting to be carried out.
Do not dump excavated earth within 1 m of excavation edge or depth of trench, whichever is more.
Do not dump excavated earth on pathways/approaches, product/steam lines, emergency facilities or OWS manhole covers.
Do not allow vehicles too close to excavation edge; maintain at least 2 m and provide anchored stop blocks.
No mechanical excavation up to 1.5 m depth from ground level in operating areas; manual excavation required up to 1.5 m.
No one should be allowed to move on the edge of excavation.

depth_limits_and_permit_escalations.requirement: Below this depth an Excavation Permit is mandatory; excavation up to this depth can be done under Cold Work Permit.
Excavation depth threshold for confined-space treatment under IS/OISD.

Aarti atmospheric gas-testing threshold.

Minimum hard-barricade height for excavations deeper than 1.5 m.

validity_and_document_control.requirement: Standard maximum excavation permit validity in normal plant operations.
Maximum excavation permit validity for shutdown units/facilities.
Maximum excavation permit validity for major construction projects.
Maximum operational duration before shift-wise renewal.

Maximum Excavation Clearance validity at construction/non-operating sites.

title: Industrial Permit to Work (PTW) System - Phase 10 Line Breaking & Blinding Extraction
source_content_markdown:
# Industrial Permit to Work (PTW) System - Phase 10 Line Breaking & Blinding Extraction

This document compiles the exhaustive safety, preparation, and positive isolation requirements for **Line Breaking, Equipment Opening, and Blinding/De-blinding** as derived from **IS 17893:2023**, **OISD-STD-105**, and **Aarti Industries (AIL) Permit Formats**.

---

## 1. WHEN THIS WORK REQUIRES A PERMIT

*   **Line / Equipment Opening**: Opening process machinery, opening vessel manways, breaking lines for strainer cleaning, changing of gauges on process equipment, and dismantling flanged joints all require authorization [4.1.4.6, 134, 187].
*   **Permit Path**:
    *   **Cold Work Permit**: Opening process machinery, blinding & deblinding, tightening of flanges, and hot bolting are performed under a Cold Work Permit [4.1, 134, 187].
    *   **Hot Work Permit**: Required if the line opening or flange breaking is a preparatory step for any spark-producing activity, or if line cutting/welding is needed [3.2.2, 135].
    *   **Vessel Entry Permit**: Required if the equipment opening leads to bodily entry [3.3.1, 182].

---

## 2. ASSOCIATED PERMITS & DOCUMENTATION

Work involving breaking containment or positive isolation must be coordinated with:
1.  **Cold/Hot Work Permits**: Formally authorizing the physical mechanical work [4.1, 4.2, 134, 135].
2.  **Confined Space Entry Permit**: Mandatory if line breaking/blinding is a preparatory step for entry into tanks or columns [3.3, 182].
3.  **Electrical Isolation Permit**: If the isolated line is connected to motorized pumps, agitators, or Motor Operated Valves (MOVs) [4.1.4.1, 4.4, 137, 186].
4.  **Blinding Diagram / Blind List**: Standard schematic drawings detailing exact blind locations and ratings [B-6.1, F-12.14].

---

## 3. EQUIPMENT PREPARATION FLOW

Before breaking any flange or containment:
*   **Operations Responsibility**: The operating department is responsible for depressurizing, draining, water washing, steaming, or gas purging the lines and equipment [4.1.6, 189].
*   **Decontamination**: Equipment must be completely washed off with cold/hot water, steamed, or purged with inert gas (Nitrogen) or air [4.1.7.1, 190].
*   **Unplugging Low-Points**: To avoid trapped pockets of hazardous liquids, all low-point drains must be unplugged during the draining phase [6.0-j, 150].
*   **Unplugging High-Points**: All high-point vents must be unplugged during steam or inert gas purging to ensure thorough sweeping of vapors [6.0-k, 151].

---

## 4. DEPRESSURIZATION, DRAINING, FLUSHING, & PURGING

### A. Depressurization
*   **Trapped Vapors**: Lines under pressure must be depressurized. The permit issuer must verify that zero residual pressure remains, ensuring that no gas or liquid pockets are trapped in inaccessible operational dead-legs [4.1.6, 6.0-j, 150, 189].

### B. Draining
*   **Closed System Draining**: Draining of hydrocarbons or hazardous chemicals must be conducted strictly within a closed system. **Draining of hydrocarbons/chemicals directly onto the floor is prohibited**, as it makes the workspace unsafe and presents an immediate fire and toxic hazard [A-7.1.5, 48, 207].
*   **Inaccessible Areas**: Special attention must be paid to liquid hydrocarbons collecting in level gauges, small nozzles, vessel bleeders, and pipe work laterals [6.0-j, 150].

### C. Flushing
*   **Water Washing**: Flushing is utilized for cleaning, cooling, gas freeing, and removing traces of aggressive acids or corrosive process chemicals [6.0-l, 152].
*   **Metallurgical Care**: Saline or sea water must not be used on sensitive metallurgy. If required, DM (demineralized) water flushing must be used to preserve structural integrity [6.0-l, 152].

### D. Purging
*   **Gas Freeing**: Displacing hydrocarbons/toxic vapors with steam or inert gas (Nitrogen). Final traces of gas are swept out using a properly grounded air eductor [6.0-k, 151].

---

## 5. TEMPERATURE & PRESSURE VERIFICATION

*   **Temperature Limits**:
    *   Work on process piping or equipment for painting must only be done at surface temperatures **below 50 ÂºC** [3.1.2-c, 4, 180].
    *   Confined spaces must be adequately cooled for safe entry [B-1-C-x, 56, 211].
*   **Pressure Check**: The issuer must physically verify that the system pressure gauge reads zero and that vents/drains are left open to the atmosphere to prevent vacuum or pressure buildup [4.1.4.1-a, 185].

---

## 6. GAS TESTING RULES FOR Containment BREAKING

*   **Pre-breaking Test**: Before containment is broken in a hydrocarbon service, a gas test is mandatory to confirm:
    1.  **Flammable Gas**: Must be **Exactly Zero (% LEL)** [6.2-b, 31, 141, 199].
    2.  **Oxygen**: Minimum **19.5% by volume** (max 23.0% vol to avoid enrichment) [6.2-a, 31, 141, 198].
    3.  **Toxic Gas**: Must be **strictly below the Threshold Limit Value (TLV)** of the specific process chemical [6.2-c, 31, 141, 199].
*   **Test Radius**: Gas monitoring for welding or hot work must be conducted within a **5.0-meter radius**, paying particular attention to nearby open drain channels, adjacent valve glands, and flange joints [6.1, 30].

---

## 7. PROCESS ISOLATION METHODS

Under **IS 17893 : 2023 Cl. 4.1.4.1** & **OISD-STD-105 Cl. 6.0-i**, process isolation can be achieved via five specific methodologies:

1.  **Single Valve Isolation**: Closing the isolation valve tight shut and keeping the vent/drain valve open between the equipment and the isolation valve [4.1.4.1-a, 14, 185].
2.  **Double Block and Bleed (DBB)**: Closing double block valves and keeping the intermediate bleed valve locked open [4.1.4.1-b, 14, 185].
3.  **Slip Blinding**: Closing the isolation valve tight shut and inserting a blind of the same rating/classification as the pipeline [4.1.4.1-c, 15, 186].
4.  **Physical Disconnection**: Physical disconnection of the pipeline attached to the equipment and blank-blinding the open active end (live end) [4.1.4.1-d, 15, 186].
5.  **MOV Isolation**: Closing the Motor Operated Valve (MOV) and physically isolating/tagging the power supply to the MOV drive motor [4.1.4.1-e, 15, 186].

---

## 8. POSITIVE ISOLATION MANDATES

*   **Reliability Warning**: **Single valve isolation (Method 1) and Double Block and Bleed (Method 2) are classified as UNRELIABLE and must not be used as standalone isolation for hot work, confined space entry, or hazardous chemical services** [4.1.4.2, 15, 186].
*   **Positive Isolation Requirement**: For all hot work and confined space entry, **Positive Isolation** (Method 3: Slip Blinding, or Method 4: Physical Disconnection and blanking live ends) is strictly mandatory [4.1.4.7, 16, 187].
*   **Long Duration Cold Work**: Positive isolation by slip blinding is mandatory for cold work if the job is planned for more than one day or is to be resumed after a work break [4.1.4.3, 16, 187].
*   **Valves Not Passing (Exception)**: If the isolation valves are tight-shut and verified as not leaking (non-passing), valve isolation *may* be accepted by the issuer for minor cold tasks like breaking lines for strainer cleaning, pump PM, or gauge changes [4.1.4.6, 16, 187].

---

## 9. BLINDING & BLIND CONTROL REQUIREMENTS

*   **Rating Matching**: Installed blinds must possess the exact same flange classification and pressure rating as the pipeline or equipment [4.1.4.1-c, 15, 186].
*   **Proximity**: Blinds must be installed as close to the vessel/equipment flange nozzle as physically possible [6.0-i, 150].
*   **Off-site Repair Blinding**: If equipment is physically removed from the plant site for workshop repairs, all remaining open process lines must be immediately end-blinded [4.1.4.4, 16, 187].
*   **Isolation Tags**: Every blind point and isolation valve must carry a physically attached, signed "DO NOT OPERATE" tag [4.1.5.1, 17, 188].
*   **Blind Logs**: A master record of all installed/removed blinds and tags must be maintained [4.1.5.1, 17, 188].
*   **Hand Over Check**: On job handover, the performing maintenance department must formally certify: *"Is isolation / blind of line removed and no obstructions?"* [AIL Hand Check Sl. 9, multimodal_86].

---

## 10. TRAPPED PRESSURE & RESIDUAL CHEMICAL SAFEGUARDS

### A. Flange Wedging Safety Rule
*   **The Flange Rule**: **"Always first wedge open the flanges"** [A-7.1.9, 49, 207]. 
*   *Why it matters*: When loosening bolts to break a flanged connection, workers must never remove all bolts immediately. They must leave bolts on the side away from them loose but engaged, and use a brass/non-sparking wedge to pry open the flange on the side facing away from them first. This ensures that any trapped residual pressure or toxic chemical sprays away from the technician.

### B. Trapped behind Linings
*   **Lining Checks**: Before undertaking hot work, a specific check must be performed to detect any hydrocarbon oil or gas trapped behind internal equipment or vessel protective linings [6.0-x, 158, 266].

---

## 11. PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)

When breaking containment on chemical/hydrocarbon lines:
*   **Chemical Splash Protection**: **PVC Suit (with or without hood)** is mandatory to protect the body against chemical or acid sprays [29].
*   **Face Protection**: A full-size **Face Shield (F.S.)** must be worn during flange breaking to prevent facial chemical burns [29, 223, 269].
*   **Hand Protection**: **PVC Hand Gloves** (resistant to process chemicals) must be worn instead of general cotton/leather gloves [269, multimodal_86].
*   **Foot Protection**: **PVC Gumboots** are mandatory for handling acids, spent acid, oleum, or caustics to prevent chemical absorption [269, multimodal_86].
*   **Respiratory Protection**: A **Cartridge Gas Mask** or **Airline Respirator / SCBA** must be used if residual toxic vapors or oxygen-deficient conditions exist [29, 222, 269].

---

## 12. RESPONSIBILITIES, APPROVALS, & RESTORATION

### A. Responsible Departments
*   **Operations Department**: Inspects equipment, performs process flushes/steaming, checks atmosphere, isolates MOVs, attaches isolation tags, and issues the permit [18, 130, 189].
*   **Maintenance Department**: Receives the permit, performs toolbox talks, executes physical blinding/de-blinding, and carries out the mechanical repair [138, 204].

### B. Signatures & Approvals
*   **Issuer (Shift In-Charge)**: Authorizes the process isolation, gas testing, and signs to issue [7.2.1, 130].
*   **Executor / Receiver**: Accepts the permit and assumes site safety custody [7.3.1, 132].
*   **Area Operator**: Attaches tags, conducts site checks, and signs to allow work to start [7.5.1, 188].

### C. Shift Handovers & Renewals
*   **Validity**: Permit is valid for a single shift (max **8 hours**) [9.1, 159].
*   **Continuance**: Next shift Area Operator must visually check isolations and sign the endorsement block to extend the permit [7.5.6, 271].
*   **Extension Limit**: Valid up to **7 calendar days** on the same permit overleaf, after which a new permit is required [9.2.6, 162].

### D. Closure & Restoration
*   **Housekeeping & Debris**: The Receiver must clear all tools, scrap, and temporary rigs [10.1.1, 204].
*   **Re-installing Protections**: Guards, gratings, and railings removed during the work must be securely re-installed and bolted down [10.1.1, 204].
*   **Isolation Removal**: The Area Operator removes "DO NOT OPERATE" tags and records the normalization of valves/blinds in the operations logbook [4.1.5.2, 188, 281].
*   **Double Signature Closure**: The permit is only officially "Closed" once both the Issuer and Receiver sign the closure section [144, 253, 271].

---

## 13. EXCAVATION / LINE BREAKING NUMERICAL SUMMARY

*   **0% LEL**: Absolute maximum hydrocarbon limit permitted for any hot work/welding [6.2-b, 31, 141, 199].
*   **5.0 m**: Radial test zone within which gas tests must be conducted near flange breaking/hot work [6.1, 30].
*   **50 ÂºC**: Maximum equipment surface temperature permitted for routine cold work painting [3.1.2-c, 4, 180].
*   **10 minutes**: Minimum wait time after shutting down forced air movers before performing gas tests [C-14.1.4, 79].
*   **24 V**: Maximum voltage allowed for temporary inspection hand lamps inside confined metal vessels [3.9, 196].
*   **7 days**: Maximum total extended lifetime of any single work permit [9.2.6, 162].
*   **30 days**: Minimum retention period for closed original permits by the issuer [13, 43].
*   **3 months**: OISD retention period for completed work permits from job completion [5.0-w].

---

## 14. UNCLEAR / ILLEGIBLE ITEMS

*   **OISD-STD-105 Page 12 Annexure-II**: Checklist Item B-1 contains a typographical spelling error: **"providing"** instead of "provided" (*"Proper ventilation and Lighting providing"*).
*   **IS 17893 Cl. 4.1.25**: Typo spells solvent as **"solven/others"** (*"...release of oil, gas or solven/others"*).

---

# PHASE 10 COMPLETE

# Industrial Permit to Work (PTW) System - Phase 26 Master Permit Decision Logic

This document compiles the exhaustive master decision-making logic, permit triggers, mandatory clearances, and compliance boundaries derived strictly from **IS 17893:2023**, **OISD-STD-105**, and **Aarti Industries (AIL)**. All rules are structured as strict **IF-THEN** statements to eliminate ambiguity in automated and manual job safety assessments.

---

## I. MASTER PERMIT DECISION LOGIC (IF-THEN RULES)

### 1. Hot Work
*   **RULE 1-A**: IF any non-routine or maintenance activity involves welding, gas cutting, burning, brazing, soldering, hot plates, tar melting, open flames, or electric arcs, THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.2.2; OISD 4.2].
*   **RULE 1-B**: IF any non-routine or maintenance activity involves grinding, mechanical chipping, shot blasting, or hacksaw cutting on lines earlier carrying hydrocarbons or chemicals, THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.2.2-a; OISD 4.2].
*   **RULE 1-C**: IF any activity requires the use of non-explosion proof (non-FLP) or non-intrinsically safe equipment (such as standard mobile phones, non-FLP cameras, or flashlights) inside operating battery limits or hazardous zones, THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.2.2-f; OISD 4.2].
*   **RULE 1-D**: IF any task requires the entry or operation of petrol/diesel-driven vehicles, portable generators, mechanical excavators (JCBs), concrete mixers, or other internal combustion (IC) engines inside hazardous process areas, THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.2.2-f.2; OISD 4.2].
*   **RULE 1-E**: IF any work occurs within a **3.0-meter radial distance** beneath or adjacent to un-insulated overhead power lines (LT/HT), THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.2.2-f.2].

### 2. Cold Work
*   **RULE 2**: IF a non-routine maintenance, construction, or civil task does not produce open flame, heat, or sparks of sufficient energy to ignite flammable mixtures, AND does not fall under specialized permits (such as height, confined space, electrical LOTO, excavation, or radiation), THEN a **Cold Work Permit** is required [IS 3.1.1; OISD 4.1].
    *   *Examples of Cold Work*: Hydrostatic testing (hydrotesting), hydro-jetting, painting (at temperatures below 50 ÂºC), insulation application, hand excavation shallower than 30 cm, offline valve gland packing (no drilling), and general mechanical bolting [IS 3.1.2; OISD 4.1].

### 3. Confined-Space Entry
*   **RULE 3-A**: IF any person must bodily enter an enclosure not designed for continuous human occupancy, having restricted means of entry and exit (including tanks, columns, reactors, boilers, boiler drums, sumps, spheres, bullets, bins, silos, column skirts, floating roof decks >3 m down, OWS pits, sewers, or tunnels), THEN a **Confined Space / Vessel Entry Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.3.1; OISD 4.3; Aarti Format No. AIL-CS/AMS/MFG/JM/TPL/PMT/03/00 Rev 05].
*   **RULE 3-B**: IF any open excavation, trench, or pit reaches a depth of **more than 1.2 meters** (under IS/OISD standards), THEN the excavation must be treated as a confined space, AND a **Confined Space Entry Permit** is mandatory [IS D-26.1.5; OISD 4.3].
*   **RULE 3-C**: IF any excavation, trench, or pit reaches a depth of **more than 1.5 meters** under the Aarti Industries safety system, THEN both an Excavation Permit and a **Confined Space Entry Permit** are mandatory [Aarti Work Instruction 1].

### 4. Electrical Work
*   **RULE 4**: IF any repair, diagnostic, installation, or maintenance work is to be carried out directly on live electrical switchgear, LT/HT feeders, power cables, substation buses, or distribution panels, THEN an **Electrical Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 4.1.15; Aarti Format No. AIL/SFT/F/29 Rev 02].

### 5. Electrical Isolation / LOTO
*   **RULE 5**: IF any maintenance task requires de-energisation of motive power, space heaters, or control circuits at the Substation/MCC panel before starting mechanical or electrical repairs, THEN an **Electrical Isolation / Energisation Permit-HT/LT (Clearance Certificate)** is mandatory [IS Cl. 3.5 & Annex E; OISD Cl. 4.4].

### 6. Excavation / Floor Breaking
*   **RULE 6-A**: IF any ground cutting, trenching, digging, or grading task exceeds a depth of **30 cm**, THEN an **Excavation Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.1.2-j, 3.4].
*   **RULE 6-B**: IF floor breaking or concrete chipping using mechanical concrete breakers is executed inside operating plant battery limits, THEN both an **Excavation Permit** and a **Hot Work Permit** are mandatory [IS 3.2.2, D-26.1.10].

### 7. Work at Height
*   **RULE 7-A**: IF any task is performed at or above a height of **1.8 meters** above ground or floor level where a permanent platform and guardrails are not provided, THEN a **Working at Height Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.1.2-k, 3.6; OISD 5.0(e)].
*   **RULE 7-B**: IF work is conducted at heights of **2.0 meters and above** under the IS/Aarti standards, THEN a full-body safety harness with double lifelines AND a valid height medical fitness certificate (Form F-20.1) are strictly mandatory [IS F-12.10, F-20.1; Aarti Instruction 3].

### 8. Fragile Roof
*   **RULE 8**: IF any task involves stepping on, repairing, or cleaning fragile roofing (such as asbestos sheets, corrugated plastic, or translucent tiles), THEN both a **Fragile Roof Permit** AND a **Working at Height Permit** are strictly mandatory [Aarti Format No. AIL/SFT/F/31 Rev 02].

### 9. Radiography
*   **RULE 9**: IF any task involves non-destructive weld testing using ionizing radiation sources (such as mobile X-ray machines or radioactive isotopes like Iridium-192/Cobalt-60), THEN a **Radiation Permit (Radiography Permit)** is strictly required [IS 3.7, Annex G; OISD 5.0(t)].

### 10. Vehicle Entry
*   **RULE 10**: IF any petrol/diesel-driven vehicle or mobile internal combustion (IC) engine must enter plant operating areas or hazardous battery limits, THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS 3.2.2-f.2; OISD 4.2].

### 11. Lifting & Rigging
*   **RULE 11-A**: IF any routine lifting operation utilizes hoists, chain pulley blocks, or cranes, THEN a **Cold Work Permit** is required [IS 3.1.1].
*   **RULE 11-B**: IF a lifting operation requires a diesel-driven mobile crane to enter or operate inside operational plant battery limits, THEN a **Hot Work Permit** is strictly required [IS B-6.14; OISD 4.2].

### 12. Chemical Handling
*   **RULE 12**: IF any task involves the manual transfer, draining, or cleaning of corrosive, toxic, or flammable process chemicals (such as sulphuric acid, spent acid, oleum, chlorosulfonic acid, DMS, caustic, benzene, methanol, or ammonia), THEN a **Cold Work Permit** is required, AND specialized chemical PPE (PVC suit, PVC hand gloves, PVC gumboots, and organic/chemical cartridge respirator) must be worn [Aarti Format No. AIL/SFT/F/08 Rev 05].

### 13. Line Breaking / Equipment Opening
*   **RULE 13**: IF any work involves opening flanged joints, blanking, blinding, de-blinding, or dismantling pipelines containing chemical, oil, steam, or high-pressure utility services, THEN a **Cold Work Permit** is required, AND positive isolation (slip blinding or physical line disconnection) is mandatory [IS 4.1.4.2; OISD 6.0(i)].

### 14. Road Cutting
*   **RULE 14**: IF any excavation or maintenance activity requires cutting, trenching, or blocking an operational plant road, THEN an **Excavation Permit** is required, AND a registered **Road Closure Document** must be submitted to the Fire Station **at least one day in advance** [IS D-25.9; OISD 6.0(v)].

### 15. Dyke Cutting
*   **RULE 15**: IF any construction or piping task requires cutting, breaching, or making an opening through a tank farm containment dyke bund wall, THEN a **Hot/Cold Work Permit** is required, AND the permit must be elevated to **Senior Management** for special authorization [OISD 5.0(v)].

---

## II. COMPLIANCE & SAFETY BOUNDARIES

### 1. Supporting & Associated Permit Triggers
*   **Confined Space Entry Preparations**: Triggers the need for a **Cold Work Permit** (for line blinding, water flushing, or scaffolding erection inside) and an **Electrical Isolation Permit** (for positive de-energisation of vessel agitators or motorized valves) [IS 125, 252].
*   **Scaffolding Erection**: Scaffolding erected for height work must be linked to the primary permit using the Table 16 associated permits block: **Hot Work / Confined Space Entry, Cold Work, Confined Space Entry, Radiography, Excavation, Electrical Isolation, or Working at Height** [IS F-15].
*   **Mobile X-Ray Radiography**: The use of a mobile X-ray machine inside battery limits triggers a **Hot Work Permit** due to non-explosion proof electrical components [IS 266; OISD 435]. If radioactive isotopes are used without electrical panels, it triggers a **Cold Work Permit** [OISD 435].

### 2. Mandatory Clearances
*   **Excavation Clearance**: Strictly mandatory for any ground cutting deeper than 30 cm. Must be signed by Electrical, Instrument, Telecom, Firewater, Product Line, and CP groups before the excavation permit can be officially authorized [IS D-8, D-25.1; OISD 5.0(v)].
*   **Road Closure Clearance**: Initial clearance must be obtained from the Fire Department before any road blockage can be approved [IS D-25.9; OISD 6.0(v)].
*   **Inter-Unit Battery Limit Clearance**: For any line opening or blinding on pipelines interconnecting two different process units, a mutual clearance signature from the **Shift In-Charges of BOTH plants** is mandatory [IS Section 8].

### 3. Mandatory Job Safety Analysis (JSA)
*   **JSA Mandate**: A formally completed and signed Job Safety Analysis (JSA) is strictly mandatory for the following operations:
    1.  Excavations deeper than 1.2 m (or 1.5 m under Aarti rules) [IS Table 14; Aarti Format 32].
    2.  Confined space / Vessel entry [IS Table 11; Aarti Format CS].
    3.  Working on fragile roofs [Aarti Format No. AIL/SFT/F/31].
    4.  Hot tapping and live process drillings [IS 4.1.20].
*   **GSA (General Safety Analysis)**: **[NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE]** - The source does not mention or define a GSA; only JSA is utilized.

### 4. Mandatory Positive Isolation
*   **RULE**: **Isolation by single closed valves or Double Block and Bleed (DBB) systems is UNRELIABLE and must never be adopted as a standalone process barrier for hot work, vessel entry, hot tapping, or hazardous chemical services** [IS 4.1.4.2; OISD 6.0(i)].
*   **Positive Isolation Mandate**: Positive isolation is strictly mandatory and achieved ONLY by:
    1.  **Slip Blinding**: Inserting solid metal slip blinds of the correct pipeline classification/rating as close to the vessel nozzle as physically possible [IS 4.1.4.2].
    2.  **Physical Disconnection**: Physically dismantling a pipe spool and blank-blinding the open active end (live end) [IS 4.1.4.2].

### 5. Mandatory Gas Testing

The Gas Safety Inspector (GSI) must perform atmospheric gas testing using calibrated portable gas detectors before permit issuance for all Hot Work, Confined Space Entry, and Leak Testing operations:

*   **Oxygen (O2) Limits**: Must be a **minimum of 19.5% by volume** [IS 56; OISD 4.3] and a **maximum of 23.0% by volume** (to prevent oxygen enrichment fire hazards) [IS 114].
*   **Flammable Gas / Hydrocarbon Limits**:
    *   Must be **Exactly Zero (0% LEL)** for any hot work, welding, grinding, hot tapping, or vehicle entry [IS 57; OISD 5.0(n)].
    *   **Max 5% LEL** is allowed for confined space entry with cold work (no hot work) without an air-supplied breathing apparatus [IS 113].
    *   **Max 20% LEL** is allowed for confined space entry *only* when wearing an approved air-supplied breathing apparatus [OISD 4.3].
*   **Toxic Gas Limits**: Must remain **strictly below the Threshold Limit Value (TLV)** of the specific process chemical (e.g., H2S limit is 10 ppm) [IS 6.2-c; OISD 5.0(n)].
*   **Gas Testing Wait-Time Rule**: If mechanical forced-air ventilation is running inside a vessel, the air mover must be shut off for **at least 10 minutes** before performing gas safety tests to ensure a static atmospheric sample is measured [IS 79, C-14.1.4].
*   **Gas Testing Radius**: For hot work, testing must cover a **5.0-meter radius** around the weld/ignition site, specifically checking adjacent valve glands, flange joints, and open drains [IS 6.1].

### 6. Mandatory Standby Person / Attendant
*   **Confined Space Entry**: A minimum of **two trained standby attendants** must remain physically stationed outside the manhole at all times while anyone is inside. They must maintain constant touch/communication and log all entrants [IS C-15 Note 2; OISD 4.5].
*   **Standby Attendant Prohibitions**: **"Do not give any other responsibility to stand by person, which may cause his absence at man way"** [IS C-15 Note 2]. They must never enter the space to perform rescue unless relieved by another standby person and wearing an SCBA [IS C-15 Note 2].
*   **Fire Standby (Fire Watch)**: A trained standby fireman must be posted near the work area for all hot work executed in operational process zones [IS B-6.19; OISD 6.0(e)].

### 7. Mandatory Rescue Arrangements
*   **Confined Space Entry**: The executing agency must keep a Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) or airline respirator, a resuscitator-inhalator, retrieval hoisting equipment/tripods, and spare full-body safety harnesses at the manhole [IS C-14.2.1; OISD 5.0(u)].
*   **Height Work**: Fall arrest safety nets must be deployed directly beneath fragile roof work. Rescue retrieval lines must be secured to independent structures.

### 8. Renewal Requirements
*   **Shift Validity Limit**: Permits are valid for a single shift (maximum **8 hours** under IS, or single shift under OISD) [IS 76, 355; OISD 293, 447].
*   **Revalidation Limit**: Permits can be renewed shift-wise on the overleaf for up to a maximum of **7 calendar days** with joint inspection and fresh gas tests [IS 79, 260; OISD 435, 449].
*   **Shutdown / Construction Turnaround Exceptions**: 
    *   Shutdown units: valid for up to **15 days** [IS 115, 376].
    *   Blanket/Construction permits: valid for up to **30 days** [IS 115, 376].
*   **Aarti Industries Confined Space Exception**: Note 2 of the Aarti Industries permit strictly prohibits the renewal of Confined Space permits: **"Renewal confined Space permit not allowed."** A fresh permit must be issued for each shift/day [Aarti Format No. AIL-CS/AMS/MFG/JM/TPL/PMT/03/00 Rev 05].

### 9. Closure Requirements
*   **Housekeeping and Inspection**: On completion of work, the Executor must remove all tools, tackles, scaffolding, and scrap, and clean the area. The Area Operator physically inspects the site's cleanliness and signs the permit [IS 81, 266].
*   **Vessel Box-Up Check**: Prior to physically boxing up any column or vessel, the Executor and Issuer must physically inspect the internals and certify that: (1) Work is complete, (2) All personnel are out, (3) No tools or maintenance gear are left behind, and (4) All debris is removed [IS Table 12; OISD 3.0(c)].
*   **Signatures**: The permit is officially closed only when **both the Issuer and Receiver sign the closing section of the permit**. Closed permits must be archived: **at least 30 days** under IS rules [IS Section 13], or **at least 3 months** under OISD rules [OISD 5.0(w)].

---

### END: PHASE 26 COMPLETE
