title: Radiography / Radiation Safety

scope: International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) guidelines
key_themes: First-response safe containment for source-stuck emergencies
SIMOPS scaffold barriers and evacuation during active radiography
research_summary.summary: The research identifies field boundary dose rates, occupational exposure limits, emergency source recovery controls, and SIMOPS exclusions for industrial radiography operations.

requirements.title: Occupational Annual Dose Limits
requirements.job_applicability: Industrial NDT field exposures using X-ray or gamma-ray sealed sources.
requirements.why_it_matters: Restricts long-term cumulative cellular damage. The annual effective dose limit for occupational radiation workers is 20 mSv per year averaged over a block of 5 years (total of 100 mSv in 5 years), with a strict ceiling of 30 mSv in any single calendar year.

requirements.title: Eye Lens Dose Limit (Cataract Prevention Amendment)
requirements.job_applicability: Daily work of NDT radiographers and RSOs.
requirements.standard_edition: ICRP 118 Statement on Tissue Reactions / AERB Amendment.
requirements.clause_section: Section on Equivalent Dose Limits for the Lens of the Eye.
requirements.why_it_matters: Protects the lens of the eye against radiation-induced tissue reactions (cataracts). The permissible equivalent dose has been strictly reduced from 150 mSv/year to 20 mSv per year averaged over defined periods of 5 years, with no single year exceeding 50 mSv.

requirements.title: Pregnant Radiation Worker Protective Relocations
requirements.job_applicability: Operational deployment of female radiation workers.
requirements.clause_section: Rule on Protection of Pregnant Radiation Workers.
requirements.why_it_matters: Protects the vulnerable embryo/fetus from birth defects. Once a pregnancy is declared, work conditions must be modified to ensure the equivalent dose to the embryo/fetus does not exceed 1 mSv during the remaining period of the pregnancy, requiring immediate relocation from field exposure tasks.

requirements.title: Controlled Area Boundary (Public Cordon-Off Dose Rate)
requirements.job_applicability: Field NDT radiography on cross-country pipelines, yards, or plant tie-ins.
requirements.source: AERB Safety Code for Industrial Radiography (AERB/SC/IR-1).
requirements.why_it_matters: Protects non-radiological plant workers and the public from stray ionizing rays. The physical cordon boundary must be established at a safe radial distance where the radiation dose rate does not exceed 1 ÂµSv/h (0.001 mSv/h), verified with a calibrated survey meter.

requirements.title: Restricted High-Radiation Boundary (Occupational Cordon Limit)
requirements.job_applicability: Siting of radiography control panels, crank stations, or remote switches.
requirements.source: AERB Safety Code for Industrial Radiography / ICRP Guidelines.
requirements.why_it_matters: Protects the active radiography operator during exposure. The radiographer must operate the crank or remote switch from a position outside the 20 ÂµSv/h (0.02 mSv/h) dose-rate boundary, utilizing local shielding where available.

requirements.title: Active Pocket Alarm Dosimeter (Bleeper) Mandate
requirements.job_applicability: Field radiography operations and source transfers.
requirements.source: AERB Safety Code for Industrial Radiography.
requirements.why_it_matters: Unlike passive TLD badges (which are processed monthly), an active pocket dosimeter/bleeper provides real-time, audible warnings of local radiation surges, instantly alerting the worker to return to a safe distance.

requirements.title: Annual Calibration of Radiation Survey Meters
requirements.job_applicability: Functional pre-work safety checks of monitoring equipment.
requirements.source: AERB Safety Code for Industrial Radiography.
requirements.why_it_matters: A faulty or uncalibrated survey meter may falsely show zero radiation, leading a worker to step directly into an active radiation field. Meters must be physically calibrated every 12 months at an AERB-accredited laboratory.

requirements.title: Emergency 'Source Stuck' Safe Recovery Protocol
requirements.job_applicability: Malfunctioning industrial gamma radiography exposure devices (IGREDs).
requirements.source: Radiological Emergency Response Guide / AERB Safety Code.
requirements.why_it_matters: If a sealed source fails to retract, workers must never touch the guide tube directly. Safe recovery requires expanding the physical cordon boundary, placing temporary lead blankets or shielding blocks over the exposed guide tube using 3-meter handling tongs, and notifying the RSO for safe retrieve-pot recovery.

requirements.title: Police and Regulatory Notifications for Lost Sources
requirements.job_applicability: Loss of custody of sealed radioactive sources.
requirements.source: Emergency Response for Radiography Incidents / AERB RPR-2004.
requirements.clause_section: Section on Loss or Theft of Radiation Sources.
requirements.why_it_matters: Missing high-activity isotopes present extreme, immediate public health and national security risks. In the event of a lost source, a written report must be submitted to the local Police Station within 24 hours, alongside immediate regulatory alerts to the AERB.

requirements.title: Process Safety SIMOPS Scaffolding Exclusions
requirements.job_applicability: Radiography on pipe racks or structures adjacent to scaffolding work.
requirements.why_it_matters: Ionizing rays easily penetrate scaffolding deck boards. Performing radiography underneath active elevated scaffolding work is strictly prohibited. All scaffold workers must be physically evacuated from the vertical line of sight before exposure begins.

Lift occurs in non-process, non-hazardous zones.

The plan must be prepared by a certified Rigging Engineer, reviewed by a Mechanical Site Engineer, approved by the Plant Asset Head (HOD) and Safety Manager, and attached at least 24 hours in advance.

requirements.permit_applicability: Hot Work Permit, Critical Lift Plan

requirements.permit_applicability: Hot/Cold Work Permit, Critical Lift Plan
requirements.job_applicability: All crane lifting operations, especially critical and heavy lifts.
requirements.standard_edition: OISD-RP-205 (Crane Operations) / BS 7121 Code of Practice for Safe Use of Cranes
requirements.why_it_matters: A trial lift requires hoisting the load 100 mm to 300 mm above the ground and holding it for 10 to 30 seconds to confirm brake holding, sling stability, load balance, and outrigger stability.

requirements.title: Ground Bearing Capacity and 100% Outrigger Extension
requirements.permit_applicability: Critical Lift Plan, Hot/Cold Work Permit
requirements.job_applicability: Mobile crane setup and positioning on unpaved or compacted soil.
requirements.clause_section: Section on Mobile Crane Stability and Outriggers
requirements.why_it_matters: All outriggers must be fully extended to 100% (unless an on-rubber chart specifically permits otherwise), with outrigger feet resting on suitable hardwood timber mats, outrigger pads, or steel plates designed to distribute concentrated reaction forces.

requirements.title: Underground Utilities Verification
requirements.job_applicability: Mobile crane setup near process blocks, pipe racks, or underground cable trenches.
requirements.why_it_matters: Outriggers exert extreme localized ground pressures. Positioning them over buried hydrocarbon pipelines, sewers, high-voltage electrical vaults, or instruments can damage services. Siting must be cross-referenced with Excavation Clearance drawings.

requirements.title: Minimum Electrical Clearances from Overhead Lines
requirements.job_applicability: Crane boom movement, pile driving, or high-mast hoisting.
requirements.clause_section: IS 17893 Annex F (Height Work) / OSHA Power Line Clearances
requirements.why_it_matters: Setback distances must be maintained: 3.0 m (10 ft) for lines up to 50 kV; 4.6 m (15 ft) for lines over 50 kV to 200 kV; and 6.1 m (20 ft) for lines over 200 kV.

requirements.title: Non-Conductive Dry Tag Lines Rule
requirements.permit_applicability: Hot/Cold Work Permit, Critical Lift Plan
requirements.job_applicability: Hoisting large structural members, long piping spools, or wind-exposed loads.
requirements.clause_section: Section on Safe Handling of Loads
requirements.why_it_matters: Dry, non-conductive fiber tag lines allow workers to control load rotation and swing from a safe distance while reducing electrical exposure risk.

requirements.title: Suspended Load Cordon and Personnel Exclusion Zone
requirements.permit_applicability: Hot/Cold Work Permit, Critical Lift Plan
requirements.job_applicability: All lifting and rigging operations.
requirements.why_it_matters: The ground footprint beneath a suspended lift must be physically cordoned with warning tape and signboards. Personnel must never stand, walk, or work under a suspended load.

requirements.title: Dynamic Wind Speed Stop-Work Limits
requirements.permit_applicability: Critical Lift Plan, Hot/Cold Work Permit
requirements.job_applicability: High elevated crane lifts, turnaround column lifting, or yard rigging.
requirements.why_it_matters: All lifting must stop if wind speed exceeds 32 km/h (17 knots / 20 mph), or lower if specified by the manufacturer.

requirements.title: Personnel Lifting (Man-Basket) Safety Constraints
requirements.permit_applicability: Critical Lift Plan, Working at Height Permit
requirements.job_applicability: Hoisting workers inside a crane-suspended work platform or man-basket.
requirements.clause_section: Section on Personnel Platforms and Man-baskets
requirements.why_it_matters: The crane must use power-up and power-lowering only. The crane's rated capacity must be de-rated by at least 50% during the lift. Workers must anchor full-body harnesses to a separate independent lifeline anchored above the hook block.

requirements.title: Annual Load-Testing and Accessories Certification
requirements.permit_applicability: Hot/Cold Work Permit, Critical Lift Plan
requirements.job_applicability: Use of slings, shackles, wire ropes, hooks, spreader beams, and chain blocks.
requirements.standard_edition: Section 29 (Lifting Machines, Chains, Ropes, and Lifting Tackles)
requirements.why_it_matters: All lifting machines and tackles must be tested and certified by a competent authority once every 12 months. The Safe Working Load (SWL) must be legibly punched, stamped, or marked on the tackle.

requirements.title: Seasonal Color Coding of Rigging Tackle
requirements.permit_applicability: Hot/Cold Work Permit, Critical Lift Plan
requirements.job_applicability: Routine and non-routine rigging operations.
requirements.why_it_matters: Visual color coding, typically updated quarterly or seasonally, allows personnel to verify that rigging equipment is currently certified. Accessories without the current color-code tag must be isolated as defective.

chemical_gas_matrix.purpose: Provides LEL, UEL, and PEL limits for gas detection during Confined Space and Hot Work. Values based on OSHA/NIOSH standards.
